source_text: Ista haeresis non recipit quasdam scripturas, et si quas recipit, et adiectionibus et detractionibus ad dispositionem instituti sui intervertit, et si recipit, non recipit integras, et si aliquatenus integras praestat, nihilominus diversas expositiones commentata convertit. Tantum veritati obstrepit adulter sensus quantum et corruptor stilus. Vanae praesumptiones necessario nolunt agnoscere ea per quae revincuntur. His nituntur quae ex falso composuerunt et quae de ambiguitate ceperunt. Quid promovebis, exercitatissime scripturarum, cum si quid defenderis, negetur ex diverso, si quid negaveris, defendatur? Et tu quidem nihil perdes nisi vocem in contentione, nihil consequeris nisi bilem de blasphematione.
thought_title: Heretics corrupt the Scriptures and make debate futile
orientation: Tertullian is describing how heretics handle the Scriptures, and then addressing a hypothetical defender of the faith who tries to argue with them from Scripture.
pass_a_gloss: This heresy does not accept certain Scriptures, and if it accepts any, it overturns them by additions and subtractions to suit the arrangement of its own teaching, and if it accepts them, it does not accept them whole, and if it presents them whole to some extent, nonetheless it converts them by inventing different expositions. The adulterating sense obstructs the truth just as much as the corrupting pen. Empty presumptions necessarily refuse to acknowledge the things by which they are refuted. They rely on the things which they composed from falsehood and which they took from ambiguity. What will you accomplish, most practiced in the Scriptures, when if you defend something, it is denied from the other side, if you deny something, it is defended? And you indeed will lose nothing except your voice in the dispute, you will gain nothing except bile from the blaspheming.

choices.english: to suit the arrangement of its own teaching
choices.why: instituti here means the heretical system or teaching, not a physical institution; 'arrangement' preserves the sense of a deliberate ordering
rejected: to the plan of their institution
for the arrangement of their school

choices.why: adulter is an adjective modifying sensus; 'adulterating' keeps the active corrupting force of the metaphor
stilus is the writing instrument, metonymy for the act of textual corruption; 'pen' is the natural English equivalent
vanae means empty or groundless; 'presumptions' matches the glossary sense of heretical self-confidence
vocative address to a hypothetical defender; 'practiced' captures the training and skill implied by exercitatissime
blasphematione is the act of blaspheming by the heretics; 'bile' preserves the physical metaphor of anger and bitterness

pass_b_english: This heresy does not accept certain Scriptures, and the ones it does accept it overturns with additions and subtractions to suit the arrangement of its own teaching. Even when it accepts them, it does not accept them whole, and if it presents them as whole in some measure, it still twists them by inventing different expositions. The adulterating sense obstructs the truth just as much as the corrupting pen. Empty presumptions necessarily refuse to recognize the very things by which they are refuted. They rely on what they have fabricated from falsehood and what they have seized from ambiguity. What will you gain, you who are most practiced in the Scriptures, when whatever you defend is denied from the other side, and whatever you deny is defended? You will lose nothing but your voice in the dispute, and you will gain nothing but bile from the blaspheming.
